notes: These data accompany the validation of the DeepRIS (Deep-learning Regression-based Identification and tracking of debriS) framework for automated debris detection and tracking in extreme flow conditions. The dataset originates from 91 medium-scale dam-break experiments conducted to investigate debris transport under varying hydrodynamic conditions, initial configurations, and material properties, including up to 240 debris elements per test. The experiments were performed to capture complex debris interactions, including entrainment, transport, clustering, and impact processes relevant to tsunami- and flash flood-like scenarios. Image sequences, ground-truth annotations, and processed trajectory data were generated using a hybrid YOLO–DeepSORT approach. These data support reproducibility of the associated study and provide a benchmark for the development and validation of multi-object tracking algorithms and optical monitoring techniques in hydraulic and coastal engineering. Please refer to the accompanying README file for detailed information on data structure, processing workflows, and usage guidelines. For further information, please contact t.hammer@tu-braunschweig.de.
